messages:
jamie: CI perf alert on PR #16142 — microbench shows a ~9% tail-latency regression vs goldens. Failing threshold for kernel-selection test.
ci-bot: perf-check failed for pr/16142 (tail_latency): baseline=23.4ms new=25.5ms diff=+9.0% threshold=+5.0%
anika: I pulled the PR and ran the microbench locally, repro'd the tail spike. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% under the same request stream.
raj: bisect points at commit 0a1b2c3 — that change adjusted batching heuristic and raised kernel selection aggressiveness for small batches.
louis: flamegraph from perf: most time in kv::prefetch -> memcpy and kernel_dispatch decision path. looks like the selector added a fallback that causes extra copies.
anika: repro script I used: ```scripts/repro_perf.sh --model tiny --seq 1024 --iters 300 --seed 42``` yields consistent +8-10% tail.
jamie: can someone try reverting only the kernel-selector tweak to confirm? if revert drops latency back to baseline, that's our culprit.
raj: quick local revert applied (reverting commit 0a1b2c3) — running CI microbench now. command: ```git revert 0a1b2c3 && ./ci/perf/run_microbench.sh --goldens```
ci-bot: perf-check (after revert) for pr/16142-revert: baseline=23.4ms new=23.5ms diff=+0.4% ✅ within threshold
louis: canary numbers look good too — kv hit-rate restored and memcpy arc gone from flame. looks like the new heuristic caused unnecessary prefetch/copy for common seq distributions.
jamie: OK let's open a revert PR and follow-up with a smaller, safer heuristic change + unit microbench to catch this class. this is a rollout blocker.
anika: opened pr/16150 (revert 0a1b2c3) and added regression notes + repro script in the description. assigning to @sre for gated rollout.
sre-bot: scheduled gated rollout for pr/16150 on next canary, will monitor tail-latency and kv hit metrics.
jamie: thanks all. follow-up action: raj + louis to instrument kernel-selector path with telemetry and add a dedicated microbench for kv-prefetch behavior with varied seq lengths. I'll file an issue for tracking.
